newsitem.title: USA: U.S. late cash distillates gain with futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. late cash distillates gain with futures.

text.p: U.S. spot distillates scored sharp gains tracking NYMEX futures late Thursday afternoon with gasoline steady to slightly lower in another day of reluctant trading amid concerns over Iraq, players said.

Prices had swayed throughout the session, first climbing on tensions in the Middle East, then sliding on profit-taking. By the end of NYMEX trading, heating oil prices had risen almost one cent, while gasoline futures ended unchanged.
Cash market discussions were generally mild, with most players reluctant to take positions with the screen so vulnerable to sharp price swings.

Traders said differentials on most Gulf Coast gasoline grades were holding steady despite reports that Amoco had shut down an 80,000-barrel per day reformer at its refinery in Texas City, Texas earlier this week.
Amoco said it was unable to comment on the reports or whether it was operating another reformer there.
"Amoco bought a lot of gasoline on Wednesday but it didn't move the market because there's more than enough supply around," one Gulf Coast trader said.
